bullets.title: META: Hedgeye adds as top long, $1,200+ PT; wall models zero Compute revenue
bullets.body: Hedgeye added META as a top long idea on 17-Jul with $1,200+ upside target from $646, noting Muse Spark 1.1 frontier benchmarks and AI capacity coming online 2H26. Separately, Hedgeye notes Wall Street models zero revenue for META Compute, while META is reportedly in talks to lease $10B in computing capacity to Anthropic over two years and exploring similar deals with other AI labs.

bullets.title: NVDA: Dark fiber buildout confirmed; SpaceX $52B GB300 order; Japan $2.4B Rubin buy
bullets.body: Wolfe confirms NVIDIA is purchasing long-haul US dark fiber (up to 100 pairs) to address GPU ecosystem bottlenecks, bullish for Ciena and Corning. SpaceX placed its first orders with Foxconn for ~13,000 NVIDIA GB300 AI servers totaling ~$52B at ~$4M each. Japan is deploying $2.4B in Nvidia Rubin chips for humanoid robotics. Kimi K3's 2.8T-parameter model requires NVL72-scale infrastructure, reinforcing large-model inference as NVIDIA's strength.

bullets.title: Semis bear market: SOX -20% from June highs; semi positioning still elevated
bullets.body: The SOX semiconductor index entered a bear market, down 20%+ from its late-June highs, with Info Tech the most net-sold US sector for six weeks — the largest cumulative selling on GS's 10-year record. HF sentiment z-score hit -0.7, historically correlating with +5.5% 1m / +12.3% 3m momentum returns. JPM maintains tactically bullish stance with hyperscaler capex as the key re-rating catalyst.

bullets.title: TXN earnings Wednesday: +11.4% Q revenue growth expected, pricing hike tailwind
bullets.body: JPM survey respondents model TXN F2Q at $5.38B (+11.4% QoQ), underpinned by two rounds of price hike letters and strong intra-quarter checks. The 3Q guide bar is set above $5.7B. DC business is annualizing $2B+. Morgan Stanley is raising JunQ/SepQ estimates on analog/industrial strength. Key bear case is 800V platform pushout and auto weakness.

bullets.title: MSFT: CLSA initiates outperform $535 PT; Azure growth could beat 41% guided
bullets.body: CLSA initiates MSFT at outperform with $535 PT (36% upside vs. FactSet avg). Hedgeye removed its MSFT short after Azure/AI data outperformed expectations in June, with Azure Foundry router showing positive trends. MS EU Semis notes AAPL's Baltra ASIC on track for C1H27 volumes.

bullets.title: GOOGL + TSLA earnings Wednesday; hyperscaler capex the #1 catalyst
bullets.body: GOOGL (est. $117B rev, $2.87 EPS) and TSLA report Wednesday, INTC Thursday. JPM sees Google 2027 capex at $325-350B (vs $250B street). MS TMT desk and GS both flag hyperscaler earnings as the pivotal test for AI infrastructure trade after a -20% SOX selloff. Google delays to Gemini 3.5 Pro on coding weakness noted separately.

bullets.title: UBS: KLAC cut to Neutral $240; TER raised to Buy $500; LRCX Buy $435; QCOM/ARM cut
bullets.body: UBS cuts KLAC PT $255→$240 (Neutral) on litho share loss/margin concerns. Raises TER $440→$500 (Buy) as test TAM could hit $19-20B by C28. Maintains LRCX $435 (Buy) on very strong FQ4/FQ1:27 outlook. Cuts ARM $470→$360 on handset weakness. Cuts QCOM $235→$190 on smartphone pricing pressure and Apple modem insourcing. PI maintained at $175 Buy.

bullets.title: MU: MS sees >$400B FCF through 2028E; data center DRAM up 40%+ Q2; 3Q ASP +25%
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley notes data center DRAM prices up 70% Q/Q in 1Q and 40%+ in 2Q; 3Q like-for-like pricing expected +25%+. MS projects MU could generate >$400B FCF through CYE2028 and buyback 40%+ of company once share repo restriction lifts 12/9/26. UBS also flags MU at atypical 0.3x NTM EV/S discount to SK Hynix, calling it a buying opportunity.

bullets.title: AMD: 2nm Venice/MI450 debut at Advancing AI Thursday; Anthropic confirmed as customer
bullets.body: AMD's Advancing AI 2026 event Thursday expected to detail 2nm Venice server CPU and MI450/MI455 AI accelerators competing with NVIDIA Rubin, plus $200B+ AI CPU TAM discussion. Separately, AMD Senior Director of AI's public GitHub YAML file lists Anthropic as a customer with maximum priority boost; still in evaluation phase with Kubernetes CI gap flagged.

bullets.title: ORCL: Multibillion-dollar data-center cost overruns; credit risk at all-time high
bullets.body: The Information reports Oracle facing multibillion-dollar cost overruns and delays at AI data-center projects, with Project Jupiter in New Mexico at risk of 1-2 year delay due to gas pipeline permitting failure and power generation plan still unapproved. Oracle's credit default swap gauge hit a fresh all-time high. CLSA initiates ORCL at hold with $145 PT.

bullets.title: NFLX: Wolfe cuts PT to $84; Phillip Capital upgrades to buy at $110; hits 52-week lows
bullets.body: Wolfe Research cut NFLX PT to $84 from $107 citing weak 2Q26 sub growth, declining TV viewing share, and P/E cut from 28x to 20x. Phillip Capital counters with a buy upgrade at $110 PT on valuation. NFLX hit new 52-week lows Friday. JPM projects 2025-28 CAGR of +12% rev, +24% GAAP EPS.

bullets.title: CMCSA: The Odyssey opens $264M globally ($124.5M domestic); AMC Q2 crushes consensus
bullets.body: Nolan's The Odyssey posted $264.1M global opening weekend ($124.5M domestic, $139.6M international), including $51.8M from IMAX. AMC reported Q2 AEBITDA of $321.4M vs consensus $202.7M; revenue $1.60B vs $1.50B; FCF $190.1M vs $23.8M consensus. Attendance surged to 71.3M from 62.8M year-ago.

bullets.title: HUBS: Wells Fargo downgrades to Equal Weight, $225 PT; premarket -2.8%
bullets.body: Wells Fargo downgraded HubSpot to Equal Weight from Overweight with a $225 PT vs. FactSet consensus of $271. HUBS was -2.8% in premarket on the action.

bullets.title: LITE: Barclays upgrades to Overweight; analyst frames $57B market cap, 105% YoY rev
bullets.body: Barclays upgraded Lumentum to Overweight. An independent analyst frames LITE at $57B market cap with ~$985M next-quarter guidance (+105% YoY), 48-50% exit gross margins, positioned at constrained 800G/1.6T optical layers.

bullets.title: LYV: UBS raises PT to $208 (from $181); 12% 2026 revenue growth, 95%+ sell-through
bullets.body: UBS raised Live Nation PT to $208 from $181 (Buy). Expects 12% total revenue growth in 2026, concert revenue +13%, sponsorship +15%. Sell-through exceeded 95% vs ~80% for peers; avg ticket $119, 19% above peers. ~20 new O&O venues by YE26.

bullets.title: DIS: UBS expects F3Q EPS $1.91 (+18% y/y), PT trimmed to $133; SVOD margins 10%+
bullets.body: UBS forecasts DIS F3Q EPS of $1.91 vs Street $1.85, FY26 EPS guidance $6.90 (+16% y/y). SVOD margins improving 350 bps to 10.1%. PT reduced from $138 to $133 based on 16x '27-28E EPS. Sports OI declines 14% on higher NBA/WWE rights.

bullets.title: BABA: Qwen3.8 Max launches (2.4T params, claims #2 to Anthropic); EU fines €550M
bullets.body: Alibaba previewed Qwen3.8 Max with 2.4T parameters, claiming second only to Anthropic's Claude 5. Shares rallied 4-5% in Asia. EU Commission fined AliExpress €550M for Digital Services Act breach. CLSA initiates ADBE outperform $300 PT. Jefferies reaffirms Buy on BABA for full-stack AI capabilities.

bullets.title: NOW: CLSA initiates underperform $72 PT (-30%); D.A. Davidson maintains Buy
bullets.body: CLSA initiates ServiceNow at underperform with a $72 PT, implying 30% downside vs FactSet avg of $139. D.A. Davidson maintains a Buy rating on NOW citing acquisition paybook expected to drive value.

bullets.title: TSM: Total US investment raised to $265B; accelerating Arizona fab on AI demand
bullets.body: TSMC CFO confirmed strong multi-year AI chip demand and acceleration of Arizona capacity buildout, lifting total US investment commitment to $265B. CFO said company is not ruling out bond issuance to fund capex. Taiwan lawmakers separately weighing a proposal to require TSMC to self-supply power for large contracts. Morgan Stanley reiterating Overweight with planned PT raise.

bullets.title: ADBE: CLSA initiates outperform $300 PT; MSFT Copilot remains enterprise default
bullets.body: CLSA initiates Adobe at outperform with a $300 PT, implying 26% upside. JPM channel checks confirm Microsoft Copilot remains the default enterprise AI tool, with Claude and Gemini Enterprise emerging but not yet driving substitution.
